children: Inspire Brands has named the head of its Dunkin' division as interim chief executive, an abrupt leadership change that comes while the fast-food giant prepares for an initial public offering.

Dunkin' President Scott Murphy will temporarily run the Atlanta-based company while longtime Chief Executive Paul Brown takes temporary medical leave, Inspire said in a message to employees, a copy of which was viewed by The Wall Street Journal. Brown, Inspire's co-founder, is recovering from a recent injury, the message said.
Murphy, who also serves as Inspire's chief brand officer, said that he will ensure the continuity of its business, and has no plans to change the company's strategy or direction.
"We look forward to welcoming Paul back when he has fully recovered," Murphy said.

Backed by the private-equity firm Roark Capital, Inspire was founded in 2018 after Arby's acquired Buffalo Wild Wings. The company is now one of the biggest restaurant holding companies in the world, with more than 33,400 locations generating $33.4 billion in sales globally. Its holdings include Arby's, Dunkin', Jimmy John's, Buffalo Wild Wings, Sonic and Baskin-Robbins.
Inspire has been preparing for an IPO for years. The company confidentially filed for an IPO in May, and it's expected to be one of the restaurant industry's biggest in years.
But Inspire is now looking at an offering as early as the end of this year, though the IPO could get moved into early 2027, The Wall Street Journal reported last month.
Brown has been integral to Inspire's growth. His tenure predates the formation of Inspire, becoming Arby's CEO in 2013 after Roark first acquired the roast-beef sandwich chain.
Inspire acquired Sonic Drive-In in 2018 and then Jimmy John's a year later. It bought Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins for $8.8 billion.
